body: What's the problem with changing the config/init file then testing on everything?

I'm having the same issue.

In my case, several of the once opened files are on `autofs` partition managed by systemd. I have set this up so my external HDD drive is lazily mounted on first access. However, when drive is not connected, every access syscall is very slow - it goes from kernel back to userspace, which has to check whether drive is connected or not before returning an error.

```
[pid 2747289] statx(AT_FDCWD, "/mnt/<redacted>/kek.sh", AT_STATX_SYNC_AS_STAT, STATX_ALL, 0x7ffc8458f6f0) = -1 ENODEV (No such device) <0.249575>
```

Almost 0.25 seconds for a single file!

It's possible to add `AT_NO_AUTOMOUNT` flag to not trigger autofs automounting. 

But I don't think checking metadata of previously opened files on exit is a good idea. How this metadata is even used, anyway?
It hard to know from this thread if this is caused by Nvim itself or some plugin. Does `:ls` show files that are in the slow paths before exiting?

> Does `:ls` show files that are in the slow paths before exiting?

issue.title: <Ctrl-O> and :ju after startup causes temporary lockup

repository.name: neovim
repository.description: Vim-fork focused on extensibility and usability

issue.body:
### Problem

Running nvim and immediately pressing `<Ctrl-O>` or issuing `:ju` command causes nvim to freeze for 20+ seconds before the jump to file occurs / jumplist appears. Thereafter, `<Ctrl-O>`, `:ju` and `<Ctrl-I>` are responsive.

The problem appears to be resolved if all the filepaths in the jumplist are available. In my case, the jumplist contains references to files like X:\dev\xyz.txt, where drive X: is mapped to a network share that is unavailable some of the time. When files on X: are available, jumplist commands on startup are immediate as expected. When X: is disconnected / offline, the problem occurs the first time jumplist commands are issued after startup.

### Neovim version (nvim -v)

v0.10.0-dev-2663+gc1c6c1ee1

### Vim (not Nvim) behaves the same?

unable to test

### Operating system/version

Windows 10

### Terminal name/version

Windows Terminal preview

### $TERM environment variable

tmux

### Installation

Nightly win64 build
